Fighter line, rotorcraft and the Barnett Shale: SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 questions Fort Worth technicians ask

Fort Worth's aerospace work is concentrated rather than scattered. Lockheed Martin Aeronautics runs F-35 final assembly at Air Force Plant 4 on the west side, next to Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base Fort Worth. Bell Textron is headquartered in the metro, with rotorcraft engineering and manufacturing across Fort Worth and Hurst, and Airbus Helicopters has its North American headquarters in Grand Prairie. Repair stations cluster around Alliance and Meacham airports. Outside those fence lines, Barnett Shale gathering lines, compressor stations and gas plants keep pipeline crews busy under API 1104. The questions below come up whenever a Fort Worth technician tries to cross from one side to the other.

Will my pipeline UT Level II carry into a shop that supplies the F-35 line?

Not as it stands. Suppliers to fighter and rotorcraft programs usually find NAS 410 written into their purchase-order quality clauses, and the requirement flows down to every sub-tier that inspects the parts. A certificate issued under an SNT-TC-1A written practice cannot meet that requirement alone. The shop's Responsible Level 3, designated in writing, reviews your training records, experience log and examination history, decides what to credit, and sets the gap training and examinations you still need. Your pipeline years count as evidence, not as a NAS 410 certification.

Why do rotorcraft shops push penetrant and magnetic particle so hard?

Gears, shafts, hubs and other dynamic components are inspected mainly with fluorescent penetrant, magnetic particle and eddy current, and the surface methods are exactly where NAS 410 expects the most additional formal training compared with what SNT-TC-1A recommends. A field technician with mostly UT and RT hours usually needs documented penetrant and magnetic particle coursework, with approved outlines and recorded hours, before an RL3 will examine them. The magnetic particle testing in aviation page shows what that work looks like, and penetrant testing training covers the theory.

Does a repair station at Alliance or Meacham work the same way?

Not necessarily. A Part 145 repair station follows the personnel standard named in its own manual and in its customers' contracts. The FAA does not certify NDT personnel; AC 65-31B accepts NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A and others. One hangar may run NAS 410 because an airline customer requires it while the next runs a written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, so read the manual before assuming anything. Uniformed maintainers at the joint reserve base work under their own service's technical orders.

Is Tarrant County College's NDT program enough to get certified?

It gives you coursework and lab time, which is valuable evidence, but no college course certifies anyone under either scheme. An employer does, after supervised experience and its own general, specific and practical examinations. Keep the outlines and hour records from any program you finish so a future RL3 or Level III can credit them.

We sell to an aerospace prime and to a pipeline operator. One program or two?

Either can work. Keep separate written practices or clearly separate sections, print the standard and revision on each certification, keep training records to the NAS 410 level of evidence, and apply the stricter vision and examination rule wherever the two documents differ. Plan the move to NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, with your customers rather than on your own timetable. NAS 410 audit documentation support covers the file preparation and review that your RL3 then approves.

Where does Atlantis fit for Fort Worth?

Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A: theory self-paced online with our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) answering questions, rehearsal in the Practical NDT aviation workplace, and the hands-on practical at your employer's facility. There is no Atlantis classroom in Fort Worth. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 for Tarrant County employers. Before enrolling, ask the RL3 at a NAS 410 employer whether outside coursework will count toward your certification. Aerospace suppliers can use aerospace NDT consulting in Fort Worth for written practices, procedures and outside agency ASNT Level III services. The full comparison is in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A, and the RL3 role is described in NAS 410 explained.
